target_customer: Pharmaceutical, medical device companies and contract research organizations running clinical trials (CIOs, data management and clinical operations leaders)
problem: Clinical trial data sits in disconnected systems, so sponsors cannot see trial status, risk and data quality quickly. Comprehend layered cloud analytics and monitoring on top of existing systems.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS subscriptions for clinical analytics

founders.name: Rick Morrison
founders.background_notes: Named as founder and CEO on the YC page and YC blog (2013); no background found in sources I opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Required integrating data from many clinical systems (Medidata Rave, Oracle Clinical, CDISC SDTM) into near real time cloud analytics; standard SaaS engineering with hard integration and compliance parts.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with customer systems and enterprise pharma relationships created stickiness, but it sat on top of larger platforms owned by Medidata and Oracle.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Saama Technologies acquired Comprehend in August 2019; the large platform vendors did not buy it.

market_need_then: In 2013 the YC blog described customers as CIOs, data management and clinical operations directors needing connected trial data; by 2017 the company reported use at five of the largest CROs and ten of the largest pharma companies.

branding.domain_note: Used comprehend.com (YC listing); the domain does not resolve from this environment, so its current state is unknown.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise and clinical; Clinical Intelligence positioning

brand_strength.rationale: Niche enterprise brand with trade press coverage of funding but no brand story; shares its name with an AWS service.

outcome_analysis: Comprehend raised a $1.2M seed, an $8.4M Series A from Sequoia in 2013, a $21M Series B led by Lightspeed in 2014 and a $15M Series C led by Eminence in 2017, selling clinical analytics to large pharma and CROs. Saama Technologies agreed to acquire it in August 2019 with undisclosed terms. Growth was steady, but the exit size is unknown, so it is not clear whether it was a strong or soft outcome.
notes: Company website did not resolve (comprehend.com blocked or dead in this session), so its current state is unverified.
